title: 2-Variable Karnaugh Maps
excerpt: The smallest possible Karnaugh map, a 2x2 grid, worked end to end and tied back to the algebra that justifies it.

content.text: Two variables means four minterms, so the smallest Karnaugh map is a 2x2 grid: one bit assigned to the rows, one to the columns. There's no room yet for a multi-digit Gray code sequence (each axis is simply 0 then 1), but the map already has the shape every larger map will share, including the split corner cell in the top-left that holds the row and column variable names.

Below is the map for F(A, B) = A OR B. Three of the four cells hold a 1. Click a 1, click another adjacent 1, then press Check group once you think you've found a legal pair. A legal group has to be a rectangular block sized 1, 2, or 4 cells here, since 2x2 is as big as this map gets.
Two groups of size 2 cover every 1 in the map: the pair where B stays 1 while A changes (giving the term B), and the pair where A stays 1 while B changes (giving the term A).
The cell where A = 1 and B = 1 belongs to both groups. Overlap is completely legal here, the goal is to cover every 1 with the fewest, largest groups, not to partition the map into disjoint pieces.

body.text: Why This Is the Same Algebra as Before

content.text: Each group of 2 cells is doing exactly what the identity from the previous tutorial does: AB' + AB = A(B' + B) = A. Grouping visually and factoring algebraically are the same operation, the grid just makes it obvious which minterms happen to differ in one variable.

body.code:
A'B + AB = B(A' + A) = B
AB' + AB = A(B' + B) = A

content.text: OR the surviving terms together and you get F = A + B back out, the exact function you started with, just derived visually instead of algebraically. For a function this small that's not a huge win by itself, but the same procedure keeps working as the variable count climbs, which is the entire point of learning it here first.
A 2x2 grid is too small to ever need to wrap around an edge, every cell already touches every other cell along at least one side. That changes at three variables.

seoTitle: 2-Variable Karnaugh Map: Worked Example and Rules
seoDescription: Learn 2-variable Karnaugh maps with a complete worked example: how to fill the grid, group the 1s, and why each group matches boolean algebra.
